result.reason: The clause reaches the fallback position and largely the preferred position: it creates a mutual greater-of cap, retains a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, includes the fallback carve-outs (assuming Sections 13 or 14 covers confidentiality), and excludes Sparkling’s payment obligations from damages. It does not expressly carve out data-protection or security breaches, so it falls short of the preferred carve-out package. More importantly, stating that all limitations in Section 15 do not apply to Excluded Claims removes not only the monetary cap but also the direct-damages and consequential-damages limitations for those claims. The playbook requires those claims to be uncapped, not necessarily exempt from the damages exclusion, so this changes more than necessary and broadens the original risk allocation. The operative language is otherwise professionally drafted.
